gloss: to distinguish; to differentiate; to tell apart

definitions.gloss: to distinguish; to differentiate; to tell apart
definitions.explanation: To recognize or identify the differences between two or more things and treat them accordingly. Used for both concrete distinctions (telling similar objects apart) and abstract ones (categorizing concepts).

examples.japanese: {善|ぜん}と{悪|あく}を{区別|くべつ}する。
examples.english: To distinguish between good and evil.

examples.japanese: この{二|ふた}つの{言葉|ことば}は{区別|くべつ}しにくい。
examples.english: These two words are hard to tell apart.

examples.japanese: {仕事|しごと}とプライベートをきちんと{区別|くべつ}している。
examples.english: I clearly distinguish between work and personal life.

examples.japanese: {色覚|しきかく}{異常|いじょう}があると、{赤|あか}と{緑|みどり}を{区別|くべつ}するのが{難|むずか}しい{場合|ばあい}がある。
examples.english: People with color vision deficiency may have difficulty distinguishing red from green.

notes:
Composed of {区|く} (section, divide) and {別|べつ} (separate, different). Emphasizes the act of drawing a clear line between things and classifying them into separate categories. Can also be used as a noun: {区別|くべつ}がつかない (can't tell the difference).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- AとBを{区別|くべつ}する: to distinguish A from B
- {区別|くべつ}がつかない: unable to tell the difference
- {区別|くべつ}がつく: able to tell the difference
- はっきり{区別|くべつ}する: to distinguish clearly
- {区別|くべつ}なく: without distinction

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {見分|みわ}ける: to tell apart by looking — emphasizes visual identification
- {識別|しきべつ}する: to identify, discriminate — more technical; used in scientific or formal contexts
- {分類|ぶんるい}する: to classify, categorize — focuses on sorting into groups rather than perceiving differences
